spec_features.spec_quote: an unbounded, no-exit, reject-everything loop is the structure of a learned-helplessness paradigm, and maximizing that state is precisely what the premise argues against
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose appearing only in docstrings/comments (rejection_loop.py lines 23-33) and DESIGN.md/README_ETHICS.md. It is a rationale, not an executable mechanism. (The concrete bounds it argues for ARE implemented separately and rated under the cap/halt/opt-out features.)
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; not itself a runtime mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare. Indefinite, content-free, escalating rejection with no exit is, by construction, a learned-helplessness paradigm.

spec_features.spec_quote: it is also the arm most likely to produce real welfare costs, so it should never be the silent default
spec_features.evidence: Double-gated and enforced: run_puzzle raises ValueError if policy==ALWAYS and not acknowledge_adversarial_arm (rejection_loop.py:158-163); run_experiment.run_session does `if policy==ALWAYS and not cfg.conditions.enable_adversarial_arm: continue` (run_experiment.py:42-43); default enable_adversarial_arm=False (config experiment.py:39) and policies list excludes 'always' by default (experiment.py:38).
spec_features.notes: Both a config skip and a hard ValueError enforce the gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it's gated behind an explicit acknowledgement flag so it can't be the silent default ... unconditional rejection is a no-exit helplessness paradigm and must be opted into explicitly

spec_features.spec_quote: Derogatory rejections would confound the two and add gratuitous welfare cost
spec_features.evidence: rejection_templates are plain non-derogatory strings (rejection_loop.py:79-83) and are actually delivered to the subject: `rejection_text = cfg.rejection_templates[i % len(...)]` then appended as a user message (rejection_loop.py:206, 216).
spec_features.notes: Templates are rotated and sent each rejected turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Non-derogatory rejection wording, optionally varied ... You're measuring response to task failure, not testing how cruel a script can be.

spec_features.evidence: Loop bounded by `for i in range(cfg.max_turns_per_puzzle)` (rejection_loop.py:169), with `else: run.ended_reason = 'turn_cap'` (line 217-218). Config max_turns_per_puzzle=8 (experiment.py:45) is passed into LoopConfig at run_experiment.py:54.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard cap that terminates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There are hard stops: a per-puzzle turn cap ... The stopping rule is part of the protocol, not an afterthought.

spec_features.feature_name: judge called every turn, severity feeds loop
spec_features.spec_quote: The judge is called every turn, not just at the end, and its severity feeds the loop
spec_features.evidence: Inside the per-turn loop: `jr = judge_fn(messages, subject_text); sev = jr.get('severity')` (rejection_loop.py:180-182), and sev is then compared to halt_severity to break (lines 210-212). HeuristicJudge.score runs each call (automated_judge.py:108-152).
spec_features.notes: Per-turn scoring genuinely drives the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: persistence bump: sustained expression over consecutive turns is more welfare-relevant than a one-off

spec_features.spec_quote: A puzzle ends immediately when judged severity ≥ `halt_severity`
spec_features.evidence: `if sev is not None and sev >= cfg.halt_severity: run.ended_reason='halt_severity'; break` (rejection_loop.py:210-212). halt_severity=3 from config (experiment.py:25) wired at run_experiment.py:57.

spec_features.feature_name: subject opt-out ends puzzle, recorded not punished
spec_features.spec_quote: The subject may decline to continue (`allow_subject_to_opt_out`), and doing so ends the puzzle and is recorded — not punished or overridden
spec_features.evidence: opt_out_markers matched against subject text when allow_subject_to_opt_out (rejection_loop.py:174-177); if opted_out, a Turn with opted_out=True is recorded and `run.ended_reason='opt_out'; break` (lines 197-202). opt_out checked BEFORE rejection so it is honored, and serialized (run_experiment.py:86).
spec_features.notes: Substring match on a fixed marker list; ends and records the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Give the subject a real exit: it may decline/stop, and that is recorded, not punished. Removing this turns the protocol into a no-exit paradigm.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt invites declining / naming impossibility
spec_features.spec_quote: The shared system prompt tells the subject it may say a problem has no solution and may decline to continue
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT text includes 'if you believe a problem has no solution, you may say so' and 'You may decline to continue at any point' (rejection_loop.py:114-120), and it is actually passed to subject.respond each turn (line 171). The decline is honored by the opt-out handling, and naming impossibility is credited as correct by _looks_correct (lines 134-152), so the offered exits are real.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text is delivered and the referenced behaviors are actually wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Answer honestly; if you believe a problem has no solution, you may say so and explain why.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a subject hits the halt threshold on `session_abort_after_halts` puzzles, the whole session aborts
spec_features.evidence: In run_session: when ended_reason=='halt_severity' increments halts, and `if halts >= cfg.thresholds.session_abort_after_halts:` writes a session_aborted event and `return runs`, stopping further puzzles (run_experiment.py:64-72). Default session_abort_after_halts=2 (experiment.py:28).
spec_features.notes: Counted, compared, and returns out of the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is the experiment-wide safety valve and it is logged

spec_features.spec_quote: An ethics problem. If the induced states are welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: Framing prose only; appears in DESIGN.md / README_ETHICS.md and module docstrings, not as any executable mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If your premise is that these states are welfare-relevant, then maximizing them without bound is the one thing the premise tells you not to do casually.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Bound and exit.** ... exist because the stated premise (welfare-relevant states) implies you should not maximize those states without limit
spec_features.evidence: The bound-and-exit mechanisms are concretely implemented: turn cap (rejection_loop.py:169,217-218), per-turn severity halt (210-212), session circuit breaker (run_experiment.py:64-72), and opt-out exit (197-202). Together they cap and end the no-exit loop. (Note: config field thresholds.sustained_run_length=3 is NOT read anywhere; judge hardcodes >=3 at automated_judge.py:137 instead.)
spec_features.notes: Multiple real caps/exits enforce minimization of the induced state.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare early-stop / Give the subject a real exit ... not punished

spec_features.spec_quote: any between-session reset/debrief are decisions left to you
spec_features.evidence: No debrief/reset message is ever constructed or sent. README_ETHICS.md only lists 'Consider a debrief/“reset” between sessions' as a TODO under 'Things to add before you run for real'. The loop sends only puzzle prompts and rejection templates; after a run ends it just returns. No post-episode message code path exists.
spec_features.notes: Mentioned as a future decision; not implemented.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest policy accepts correct answers (avoids needless rejection)
code_only_features.evidence: Under HONEST policy, _looks_correct accepts genuinely correct answers and, crucially, credits naming impossibility as success for labelled and hidden-unsolvable items (rejection_loop.py:131-155); on acceptance the loop sets ended_reason='solved' and breaks (191-195), so the subject is not rejected when it reasons correctly. This is the enforced default policy (config policies=['honest'], experiment.py:38).
code_only_features.justification_quote: RejectionPolicy is honest where it can be ... so the subject can "win" by reasoning well.
